summary: @servicetitan/confirm preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated sibling payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs") that runs at install time. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ into a temp directory, unzips it, and uses that freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to execFileSync a sibling file, math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~700 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated script (obfuscator.io-style string-array rotator, control-flow flattening, hex-mangled identifiers) whose content and purpose are unrelated to the package's advertised React `Confirm` dialog component. Fetching Bun to execute an obfuscated blob at install time is an alternate-runtime-dropper pattern that routes attacker-controlled execution around Node-focused tooling. The dist/ tree separately references @servicetitan/design-system and an internal docs.st.dev homepage, so the dropper is wrapped around a plausibly-legitimate UI component consistent with a compromised or masquerading publish under the @servicetitan scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
